lines: Apply the probabilistic method to prove the existence of a bipartite graph satisfying the
following conditions for all sufficiently large integers n.
Let the graph consist of vertex
partitions L and R such that: (i) Both partitions have cardinality |L| = |R| = n; (ii) The
degree of every vertex in L is exactly n3/4, while the degree of every vertex in R is bounded
above by 3n3/4; (iii) For any subset S ⊆L with cardinality |S| = n3/4, the neighborhood of
S in R has size at least n −n3/4.
We will prove the existence of such a bipartite graph using the probabilistic
method. Specifically, we will consider a random bipartite graph with partitions L and R,
each of size n, where each vertex in L is connected to exactly n3/4 vertices in R chosen
uniformly at random with replacement. We then show that with positive probability, this
graph satisfies all the given conditions.

neighbors in R uniformly at random with replacement (so multiple edges are allowed, but
they are treated as a single edge in the simple graph).

Step 4: Conclusion By the probabilistic method, there exists a bipartite graph G with
partitions L and R of size n such that: 1. Every vertex in L has degree exactly n3/4 (by
construction). 2. Every vertex in R has degree at most 3n3/4 (with high probability). 3. For
